courseTitle: 100 Days of Code: JavaScript Data Structures and Algorithms

lectures.title: Why are Data Structures and Algorithms important?

cues.en: Now the question is why data structures and algorithms are very important.
Now, as a software developer or computer scientist, our responsibility is to perform the operations
on data.
We are taking data as an input, then we are processing it.
Then we are giving back the processed data as an output.
Now the input can be in any format.
For example, when you search for a direction in a Google map, you can provide the starting and the
destination points as an input to the Google map.
Then it's going to process the data to find the shortest path between these locations and provide it
to us as an output.
Now, to make this process efficient, we need to optimize all these three steps.
It's very obvious that we can optimize the second step where we have the data structures and algorithms.
So by using, for example, graph data structures and Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm, Google Map
is able to find the shortest path between the provided points very efficiently.
So this means that when we are processing the data, this is the only step where we can increase the
efficiency of our program.
So by choosing the right data structure and algorithm, we can increase the efficiency of our program,
which is going to help us to make it faster.
So let's look at another example.
So we have said that data structures refer to the way we organize the information on our computer.
And this has a great impact on performance.
So suppose you have to find a book on algorithms from the library.
Now to get it.
First you need to go to the computer science section.
Then from there you can go to the algorithms and find the book.
Now it's very easy to find the book in this case.
On the other hand, if the books are not organized in this manner and just distributed randomly, it
will be almost impossible to find the book that we need.
This is the way a librarian organizes books into particular form to efficiently perform a task.
Here books are the data, and arranging them is a data structure.
And for finding the book, we need an algorithm.
Thus, you can easily see how important data structures and algorithms are to make our program efficient
and fast.
In this manner, computer scientists process and look for the best way to organize the data so it can
be processed based on the input provided.
Now the second question is why do most companies ask questions during the interviews related to data
structures and algorithms.
It's very clear that solutions to many problems that are related to software development can be found
on the internet, or you can use some AI models to generate some codes for you by just copying and pasting
someone's code without understanding the logic behind it.
It's not possible to become a professional software developer, so by asking questions related to data
structures and algorithms, the interviewer checks the problem solving ability of the candidate.
For instance, even though today's computers come with more memory, if the developer does not handle
memory management technique, the program may leak and lose the memory.
This means that without understanding the data structures, the code may end up with a memory leak.
Now, the second reason for this is that the interviewer has limited time to evaluate a candidate.
So by asking such questions, an interviewer can evaluate fundamental concepts of programming.
This means that if a candidate is good at data structures and algorithms, he or she can learn any technology
or programming language easily.
He or she just needs to learn the syntax of the programming language.
And if you know the fundamentals of programming, it's very easy to learn any programming language.
So hopefully with this you understand why data structures and algorithms are important in programming.
